hints: Focus on how an ester splits during hydrolysis, with one part becoming the acid (or its salt) and the other becoming the alcohol.

Split $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$ at the $\text{CO}_2$ link, the left side $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$ comes from propanoic acid and the right side $\text{CH}_3$ comes from methanol.
Remember boiling with $\text{NaOH}$ gives the sodium salt of the acid plus the free alcohol, so pair the propanoic acid part with sodium.
walkthrough:
**Recall alkaline hydrolysis of esters**

Think of this as splitting the ester with a base. It is also called saponification.

Chemical equation rule:
$$\text{RCOOR' + NaOH} \rightarrow \text{RCOONa + R'OH}$$

**Split this ester into its two parts**

Look carefully at $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$. Break it at the $\text{C-O}$ bond of the ester link.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO-OCH}_3$$
The $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$ fragment is the acid part from propanoic acid. The $\text{OCH}_3$ fragment is the alcohol part from methanol.

**Form the alkaline products**

With aqueous $\text{NaOH}$, the acid part becomes its sodium salt and the alcohol part becomes the free alcohol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Na} + \text{CH}_3\text{OH}$$
That is sodium propanoate plus methanol, so sodium propanoate is one product.

options.A: Ethanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, would only form if the alcohol part was ethyl, $\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Here the alcohol part is only $\text{OCH}_3$, which gives methanol, not ethanol.
options.B: Propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, would only form if the alcohol part was propyl. The $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2$ in this ester belongs to the acid side, not the alcohol side, so this is a common mix-up of the two sides.
options.C: Sodium methanoate, $\text{HCO}_2\text{Na}$, comes from methanoic acid, $\text{HCO}_2\text{H}$. Our acid part is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ (propanoic acid), which has three carbons, not one.
options.D: The acid part $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$ is propanoate. Under alkaline conditions it is neutralised to its sodium salt, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{Na}$, which is sodium propanoate. This matches the alkaline hydrolysis products perfectly.
